title: quantization-nan-debug-scratchpad-int8-fp8-bf16
content:
Goal: track investigation into NaNs/quality regressions after enabling INT8/FP8 profiles for rw-infer serving runtime. Scratchpad + breadcrumbs for commands tried, hypotheses, quick tests, and next steps.

Background:
- After enabling int8 quantization profile (auto-calibrated, per-tensor symmetric) for customer workload, we saw intermittent NaNs in logits during long-context (>1024) runs. Issue appears ~10-30% through 2048 token generation on some prompts, not all.
- Affected models: rw-7b-v1 and rw-13b-v0 quantized with our internal int8 toolchain (kernel=fastgemm, kv-cache kept in fp16). FP8 profiles (e4m3) were also tried, showing fewer NaNs but worse quality on some prompts. BF16 run (mixed) had no NaNs but higher latency/cost.

Quick repro commands (local-ish):
- baseline fp16 (no quant):
  python -m rw_infer.run --model rw-7b-v1 --dtype fp16 --max-tokens 2048 --prompt-file tests/prompt-issue-21.txt

- int8 quant (runtime flag):
  python -m rw_infer.run --model rw-7b-v1 --quantize int8 --quant-kernel fastgemm --kv-cache fp16 --max-tokens 2048 --prompt-file tests/prompt-issue-21.txt

- fp8 (e4m3) tried:
  python -m rw_infer.run --model rw-7b-v1 --quantize fp8_e4m3 --kv-cache fp16 --max-tokens 2048 --prompt-file tests/prompt-issue-21.txt

Observed error snippets:
- Softmax overflow leading to NaN in attention: (from runtime logs)
  WARNING: attention softmax produced Inf -> downstream logits NaN
  ...
  tensor([nan, nan, nan, ...], device='cuda:0')

- CUDA kernel/illegal memory examples after a NaN appears:
  RuntimeError: CUDA kernel failed (unrecoverable)
  (stack trace pointing into fused_attention_cuda.cu: blk_softmax)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Quantization numeric range mismatch for attention logits: per-tensor scale too aggressive -> overflow in exp(softmax) for long sequences (accumulation error).
2) KV-cache stored in fp16 loses precision across long recurrences causing softmax input distribution shift and eventual overflow.
3) Fused kernels (fastgemm / fused-attention) assume no NaNs and lack appropriate clamping; quantization introduces out-of-range values that trigger GPU undefined behavior.
4) Calibration dataset for int8 is skewed relative to production prompts -> calibration scales not robust for long tails.
5) FP8 dynamic range differences cause fewer NaNs but worse token quality because exponent biases differ.

Short experiments & results:
- Switch to keeping KV-cache in fp32 (runtime flag kv-cache fp32) -> NaNs went away in 10/10 runs locally for the failing prompt, but latency + memory increased ~1.6x. Suggests hypothesis #2 is likely contributor.
- Clamp logits before softmax (runtime clamp to +-80) -> prevented NaNs in lab runs. Implementation: add safe_clip(logits, -80.0, 80.0) just before softmax in attention kernel path. This is a bandaid; still need root cause.
- Disable fused attention kernel (use reference kernel) -> no NaNs observed, but 2x slower. Points to fused kernel sensitivity (#3).
- Re-calibrate int8 scales using a longer tail of prompts (include long sequences) -> reduced frequency of NaNs but did not eliminate.
- FP8 (e4m3) runs: fewer NaNs but hallucination/quality regressions on specific prompts (weird token repetition).

Commands for quick checks I used with small harness:
- reproduce with deterministic RNG: python -m rw_infer.run --model rw-7b-v1 --quantize int8 --seed 42 --deterministic True --max-tokens 2048 --prompt tests/prompt-issue-21.txt
- run with kv-cache forced fp32:
  python -m rw_infer.run --model rw-7b-v1 --quantize int8 --kv-cache fp32 --max-tokens 2048 tests/prompt-issue-21.txt

Notes on instrumentation added:
- Added NaN/Inf detector that logs first occurrence: layer id, timestep, dtype, location (pre-attn/post-attn) and upstream activation name. Logs sent to trace-log (json-lines). Enabled temporary extra check in runtime: assert isfinite(all activations) with per-layer backoff to avoid aborting serving.
- Added histogram dumps for pre-softmax logits for failing runs. Observed occasional extreme positive outliers ~1e4 in int8 runs.

Micro root cause ideas to pursue:
- Why do float16 KV accumulations diverge more under quantized matmuls? Possibly because quantized matmul outputs are dequantized into fp16 with limited range -> small relative errors accumulate into attention weights. Need to inspect accumulation path: int8 matmul -> accumulate into fp32/ fp16? Our kernel uses fp16 accumulation for speed (fastgemm). Test toggling accumulation dtype to fp32.
- Fused attention kernel may perform in-place ops that bypass NaN-checks; combined with aggressive per-tensor scales, small rounding -> large exponentials. Need to review cuda code: softmax implementation, clamp behavior.

Immediate next steps (low friction):
- Force kv-cache to fp32 for customers experiencing NaNs and provide FAQ + mitigation steps (config flag).
- Add runtime safe_clamp for logits as emergency toggle (configurable).
- Re-run calibration job with bigger/longer prompt sample set and produce new scales; ship to canary.
- Run ablation: int8 matmul with fp32 accumulation (if kernel supports) vs fp16 accumulation. Compare memory/time vs NaN frequency.
- Add a canary job that runs 1000 long-prompt inferences per night with int8/kv-fp16 to measure NaN frequency and correlate with prompt features.

Longer-term/engineering work:
- Fix fused kernel to include robust clamping or to use fp32 accumulation for attention logits. Might need kernel rewrite or patch to fastgemm/fused-attn.
- Improve calibration pipeline: include long-tail sequences, per-head/per-row quantization options, and outlier clipping heuristics.
- Add a runtime health check that can switch KV-cache dtype to fp32 automatically on detecting rising NaN rates for a tenant.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Check PR #482 (linked) for recent fused-attn kernel changes (Elena).
- Talk to Tom about whether bf16 support in runtime uses fp32 accumulation anywhere.
- Add unit test: synthetic case that drives attention logits to extreme values using crafted input to validate clamps.
- Create customer advisory draft for KB: explaining kv-cache fp32 toggle + expected perf impact.

Raw snippets from trace-log (trimmed):
{"time":"2024-11-28T03:12:45Z","layer":"attn.6","step":1123,"dtype":"float16","pre_softmax_max":1.2e4,"post_softmax_has_nan":true}
{"time":"2024-11-28T03:12:45Z","error":"NaN detected at attn.6 step 1123","run_id":"canary-20241128-7b-int8"}

Contact: @Elena or @Tom if you need GPU kernel context. If this doc is stale, check branch quant-kernel-fixes in PR #482.

Bottom line: immediate mitigation is to prefer kv-cache fp32 or clamp logits; root fix likely in fused kernels or accumulation dtype. Need more tests to isolate int8 matmul accumulation path.
